newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed down from the day's highs on Wednesday after a volatile session which saw both a small decline and a big rise.
Share prices slipped at the outset as bonds fell, dogged by worries that the 25 basis point U.S. interest rate rise on Tuesday might give scope for a further tightening this year.

Big gains on German and Swiss bourses, mingled with shortcovering after recent falls, boosted the AEX index to its day's high of 740.84. But a weak Wall Street opening left the AEX well back from the peak with a 6.56 point gain to 734.40. "We were caught out a bit by today's gains," a dealer said.

"There's no way our market should have gone up so much today, especially after rising 12 points yesterday. It all looked a bit speculative again but there is still an awful lot of liquidity to come into this market," the dealer said.
"It looked suspiciously like a bear squeeze," said another.
The AEX last week slumped to within a whisker of 700 after Fed chairman Alan Greenspan made comments seen as paving the way for Tuesday's Federal Reserve interest rate rise.
Dealers said there was some feeling earlier on that the Fed may raise interest rates again this year. "It didn't help having strong U.S. durable goods figures today," a dealer said.
"Every time you get a figure like that it makes people start talking about an interest rate rise, we're still living in a nervous market for the time being," he said.
Other dealers said there was talk that a large U.S. bank had become bullish about Dutch stocks and that investors had been drawn back into the market because of that.

A 3.60 guilder gain in Philips to 87.00, helped boost the overall market. "There hasn't been anything new that I can think about, although there was a magazine interview with (chairman) Cor Boonstra which went back over the break-up value that might have had some influence on the stock," an analyst said.

Fortune Magazine's March 31 issue carries a lengthy interview with Boonstra in which the article points out previously voiced comments from analysts that the break-up value of the stock is higher than its recent share price.
Dealers said the shares had also been boosted by a gain in U.S. high technology stocks on Tuesday.

Fortis Amev closed unchanged at 71.50 guilders as a rise 1996 results came in line with expectations. Its forecast of higher 1997 earnings per share had also been anticipated. Other financials saw ING 40 cents higher at 72.20 guilders. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5014
